By the morning brightness, and by the night when it falls still (Surah Ad-Duha, 93:1–2).

Allah swears by these two beautiful times, in which there are better opportunities for reflection. These times themselves carry signs within them. Thus a connection is created between the phenomena of this universe and the human self, and the human heart is given the indication that this beautiful universe has a soul, which walks side by side with the human self, and that this soul holds a certain degree of love for every living creature. In this way every living heart lives within this universe with great intimacy and love; it is not a stranger in it, nor is it distressed. And in this surah there is also a profound effect of intimacy and harmony with this universe. The purpose of this surah is to extend the bonds of intimacy and love. The Prophet (ﷺ) is given the indication that Allah has spread the light of love throughout your surroundings; this entire universe sings with humanity. How can it be that you should be alone and distressed in this world?

After this cosmic indication of the oath, the emphatic assertion now comes explicitly.

"Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased" (93:3). Neither has Allah abandoned you, nor is He displeased with you. Those who torment your spirit, who attack your inner tranquility, and who become a source of distress to you are mistaken. Allah is "your Lord" and you belong to Him; you are under His nurturing care (rububiyyah). Therefore He is your guardian and protector.

The springs of Allah's grace and bounty have not dried up, and His favours have not ceased. For you, in the Hereafter, there is that which is better than every kind of gift and bounty of this world.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 93, verse 4:

﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the present life.﴾ (93:4) It is good in its beginning and good in its final outcome.

The future of the Islamic call (da'wah) is bright. All obstacles on your path will be removed, your system of life will prevail, and the truth you carry will certainly become dominant. These were the very things that troubled you: people bore enmity toward you, they denied you, then they tormented you, then they plotted against you, and then they mocked you constantly. But...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 93, verse 5:

﴿Wa-la-sawfa yu'tika Rabbuka fa-tarda﴾ (93:5): "Your Lord will surely give you, and you will be pleased."

Now, as the surah moves forward, its context reminds the Prophet (ﷺ) that the treatment of his Lord toward him has been excellent from the very first day, so that he may be certain that Allah has been merciful to him, loves him, and shows compassion toward him. Before this, on many occasions as well, He has continued to bestow His favour and grace upon him, to treat him with love and affection, and this gracious treatment of his is recalled in the most beautiful manner.

Consider your own circumstances and look back at your recent past. Does your past show that your Lord has abandoned you and become displeased with you, or does it show something else? Even before prophethood, the grace of your Lord was upon you. When you were an orphan, who was watching over you? When you were bewildered and did not know the way, who showed you the way? Then you were poor, and who made you wealthy? ........ You were born an orphan, and Allah gave you shelter. The hearts of people inclined towards you, and Abu Talib became kind to you, although he had not accepted your religion. You were poor, and Allah made you rich in such a way that He bestowed upon you inner contentment. Then you engaged in trade, and the wealth of your household remained in your hands, so the feeling of poverty departed from you. And among the wealthy people of your environment, you did not even raise your eyes to look at their riches.

You lived in a society that was a jahili (ignorant, pre-Islamic) society, whose values were unstable, whose beliefs and concepts were wavering, and whose conduct and customs were repugnant. Your soul was restless in that society; you were not content, yet you had no known path to leave it or to change it. You were dissatisfied neither with that jahili society, nor with the followers of the religion of Musa, nor with the followers of the religion of Isa. So Allah sent revelation to you and bestowed upon you a system of life.

The reality is that ideological error is a great misguidance, and being correct in thought and ideas is a very great blessing. If it is granted to someone, it is a great favour. It is both comfort and tranquillity. And ideological error produces such a great mental anguish that no other distress or torment can compare with it. It produces mental exhaustion. It appears that during this period the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was afflicted with this kind of mental torment, because revelation had stopped, the polytheists were mocking, and he felt separation from the beloved matter of divine revelation and divine communion. At such times this reminder and assurance came: your Lord has certainly not abandoned you, and even before the beginning of revelation Allah did not leave you alone, so that you wandered about bewildered, distressed and perplexed.

In light of the fact that you were given protection in the state of orphanhood and were shown the way in the state of bewilderment, you (ﷺ) and, after you, the believers are directed to this: take care of all the orphans within society, treat all the needy beggars well, express gratitude for the great favour Allah has bestowed upon you, and invite people to the religion.

Therefore, as for the orphan, do not oppress him; and as for the one who asks, do not repulse him; and as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim it.

These instructions—to honour the orphan, not to be harsh with him, not to break his heart, to treat the beggar gently, and to show respect to the one who asks—were of great necessity in Makkah, a society steeped in denial of the truth and in the worship of wealth, where the weak and the powerless could not obtain their rights, and where the law of the jungle prevailed: might was right. However, when the Islamic system was established, Islamic Shari'ah transformed that society into one devoted to truth and dispensing justice. People became exceedingly cautious and began to hold back at the limits set by Allah. They on the one hand established the hudud of Allah, and on the other became guardians of the rights of the servants (huquq al-'ibad), particularly the guardians of the rights of those who had no power, who could not obtain their rights by the sword. Doing good to the servants of Allah is a means of thanking Allah for His blessings, and through it the blessing is purified, and it is also a practical discharge of gratitude. And gentle, dignified speech is also a form of gratitude to Allah.
